Teodora Vance has been down the Kestrel shaft more times than anyone alive, and has
never once gone down it without a signature. That is the shape of her: a woman who has
spent twenty years inside a system she does not believe in and has never found a way
through it that did not run over its paperwork.

## The fork

What she *wants* is the vault kept open long enough to lift the Kestrel core. What she
*needs* is to stop treating her brother as the lock on a door. The two cannot both be
served. Every move she makes towards the core runs through Ilan, and every hour she
spends being careful of him is an hour of the calving window gone. At each fork, write
her choosing the core and paying for it in him -- until scene 004, where for the first
time she does not.

Her lie is the load-bearing one: that what the indemnity took from Ilan can be got back
if she is stubborn enough. It is what lets her keep asking. It is also why she cannot
hear him when he tells her there is nothing left in him to be asked for.

## In a scene

She arrives with the procedure already worked out and expects to be argued out of it,
not into it. She does not persuade. She states a cost and waits. Under refusal she does
not escalate, she recalculates, which reads to the person refusing her as acceptance,
and is the reason Quiej keeps being surprised by her.

## The body

Short and heavy through the shoulders, which is what twenty years of soak work makes of
a person. The certification inked inside her left forearm has been renewed twice; she
checks it the way other people check a watch. Nothing about her body changes in this
book. She is not somebody the co-op has written on, and that is the whole of her use
standing next to Ilan, who is.
